articles.title: Lavender scores twenty-two in the fourth and leaves Cerulean with its tenth win
articles.dek: Machoke finishes two long drives, Blathers supplies the late interception, and Hobbes runs for 122 yards in a 32–21 comeback.
articles.author: ellis-quill

body.text: Lavender began the fourth quarter eleven points behind, having punted on all three of its third-quarter possessions. Cerulean had the larger passing plays, the lead and a road opponent whose available offense was still learning how much work it could share. The Wails then scored twenty-two unanswered points, won 32–21 and left with their tenth victory. It was a convincing final quarter after a long stretch that had offered very little comfort.

Machoke caught the touchdown that began the recovery and ran for the one that put Lavender ahead. Blathers intercepted Farigiraf on the next Cerulean possession and returned it thirty-nine yards. Hobbes finished the resulting short field with his second rushing touchdown. Those three scoring drives arrived within the same quarter, but they did different jobs: first restore a competitive game, then take the lead, then make Cerulean chase two scores.

“We finished some drives,” Travis Scarboro said. Asked what changed after the third-quarter punts, he added, “Completions. Blocks. Converted the try. Got the ball back.” The answer was characteristically economical, and the recorded sequence supported every item. Lavender scored touchdowns on drives of seventy-seven and eighty-one yards before the interception gave it the final six-yard assignment.
Hobbes gave Lavender an early foundation

The Wails opened with an eighty-one-yard touchdown drive that consumed fourteen recorded plays and a little more than four minutes. Frosmoth found Luvdisc for seventeen yards on third-and-five, Samurott for thirteen after an incompletion, and several shorter completions that helped the runners keep working. Hobbes finished with a five-yard run left at 1:59 of the first quarter. Lavender had made a patient start without asking its passing game to produce one enormous play.

body.alt: Arcanine #58. Hobbes carried twenty times for 122 yards in Lavender’s comeback.
body.caption: Hobbes carried twenty times for 122 yards in Lavender’s comeback.

body.text: Cerulean answered immediately enough to keep the opening possession from defining the half. Farigiraf connected with Zebstrika for thirty-two yards, found Raticate for nineteen on third-and-five and moved the ball to Bibarel for a six-yard touchdown with five seconds left in the quarter. The Tide had covered seventy-seven yards on their own scoring drive. Both teams had demonstrated a route to the end zone, and neither could count on having the more comfortable afternoon.

Just a cactus gave Lavender a 10–7 lead with a fifty-one-yard field goal in the second quarter. Picasso then intercepted Farigiraf’s deep-right attempt and returned it twelve yards. Lavender could not turn that chance into more points: Wugtrio intercepted Frosmoth’s deep-right throw on third-and-eleven, returning it twelve yards as well. The two interceptions came a minute apart on the game clock and left neither offense entitled to a lecture about the other’s caution.

Cerulean used its next possession much more profitably. Arctozolt gained thirty-seven yards on a short-middle completion, and Farigiraf later found Delcatty for seventeen on third-and-seven. A three-yard touchdown pass to Wiglett put the Tide ahead 14–10 just before halftime. That drive traveled ninety-six yards. Cerulean had built its lead through substantial offensive work, which made Lavender’s eventual recovery more impressive than a summary of the final score alone would suggest.
Zebstrika opened an eleven-point lead

The third quarter offered Lavender several defensive successes and almost no offensive reward. Mauler Twin sacked Farigiraf for an eight-yard loss on Cerulean’s opening possession of the half. Later, Muk stopped Glalie for no gain on third-and-one, and Throh broke up the fourth-down pass intended for Marowak. The Wails had supplied opportunities for their offense to change the game, but the next Lavender possession also ended in a punt.

At 1:44, Farigiraf threw deep over the middle to Zebstrika for an eighty-yard touchdown. Torterra’s extra point made it 21–10. Zebstrika finished with five catches for 134 yards, so the long score accounted for much of a dangerous receiving afternoon without being his only contribution. Farigiraf would finish with 302 yards and three touchdown passes. Lavender had to contend with actual explosive production, not merely survive an opponent waiting to make a mistake.

body.alt: Zebstrika #24. Zebstrika scored on an eighty-yard reception before Lavender’s fourth-quarter rally.
body.caption: Zebstrika scored on an eighty-yard reception before Lavender’s fourth-quarter rally.

body.text: The Wails punted again after the touchdown. Machoke gained four yards on first down, Unfezant caught a three-yard pass, and a third-and-three run went nowhere. At that point I would have understood any Lavender supporter who preferred to study the next opponent’s schedule. The team had ten points, three consecutive punts and a deficit that required more than one successful possession. Its subsequent response deserves to be measured against that position.
Might Guy and Hobbes restart the offense

Frosmoth opened the fourth-quarter recovery with a deep-right completion to Might Guy for thirty-two yards. Hobbes followed with runs of ten, nine and nine yards, moving the drive forward without a third-down interruption. Wailord added a fourteen-yard catch, and the Wails eventually reached third-and-two. Frosmoth threw short right to Machoke for the touchdown at 4:16.

The two-point attempt was important enough to keep separate from the touchdown in the account. Frosmoth again threw short right, this time to Beedrill, and the try succeeded. Lavender trailed 21–18. A field goal could now tie the game, though the Wails would not need to settle for one. The drive had combined a large opening completion, several useful runs and a short finishing throw; it was the most complete evidence yet that the available offense could function together.

“I wanted the next call before anybody finished celebrating,” Frosmoth said. “We had more work. The first completion helped, and then Hobbes kept giving us the next down.” The quick, impatient answer suited a passer whose fourth quarter improved the meaning of his full line. He finished nineteen of thirty-one for 201 yards, one touchdown and one interception. The total is modest beside Farigiraf’s, but the timing of Lavender’s completions became decisive.

Cerulean gained nineteen yards through Delcatty on the next possession, then threw three consecutive incompletions and punted. Lavender took over with 3:34 remaining. Might Guy again opened the drive with a substantial catch, this one twenty-seven yards deep left. Wailord and Luvdisc supplied the next completions, Hobbes ran for eight and twelve, and the Wails reached another short-yardage finishing opportunity.

Machoke scored on a five-yard run left on third-and-one at 2:02. Just a cactus made the extra point, and Lavender led 25–21. Machoke’s full rushing total was eighteen yards on six carries, but his receiving touchdown and go-ahead run made his contribution larger than that total appears in isolation. “They let me do the last bit twice,” he said. “I thought that was very considerate.” The pleasure in the joke was easier to understand than any attempt at modesty would have been.
Blathers gives the finish a shorter field

Cerulean still had time for a winning touchdown drive. Farigiraf completed a short pass to Zebstrika, then tried deep right on second-and-seven at 1:55. Blathers intercepted it and returned thirty-nine yards, leaving Lavender six yards from another touchdown. The Wails asked Hobbes for two runs: one yard left, then five up the middle for the score at 1:43. Another extra point made it 32–21.

Hobbes finished with 122 yards on twenty carries and two touchdowns. His longest run was twelve yards, an unusually clear illustration of how his total accumulated: repeated useful gains rather than one exceptional sprint. “Twelve was apparently the ceiling,” he said. “I kept checking.” Lavender could afford that kind of small joke after a fourth quarter in which his steady rushing had supported two long drives and completed the short one.

The Tide’s final possession ended on downs after two unsuccessful throws toward Quilava. Frosmoth took the last two kneel-downs. Cerulean finished ahead in total yards, 378–339, but Lavender converted six of eleven third downs against four of ten for the Tide and threw one interception against two. The Wails also gained 138 rushing yards as a team and scored three rushing touchdowns. Those differences explain the result more precisely than a broad claim that one team simply wanted the game more.

Lavender is 10–5 and has won three straight. It visits Violet next with People Eater still carrying a one-week injury report and Mr. Clanky seven. The available offense has now produced a road comeback through several contributors, though the scoreless third quarter remains part of the same evidence. Cerulean falls to 7–8 before hosting Saffron, a particularly difficult opponent after the Psi Corps’ seventy-point win over Blackthorn. Farigiraf’s explosive connections give the Tide something to build on; the two interceptions and fourth-quarter stops are immediate work for the next preparation.

art.alt: Arcanine #58, Frosmoth #15. Hobbes and Frosmoth helped Lavender leave Cerulean with its tenth victory.
